one_liner: Cloudflare has a broad REST API with self-serve API tokens on a free account, OAuth client registration, and an official MCP server covering the whole API.
auth_notes: API tokens (Bearer) are the recommended, documented method. The legacy Global API Key is sent as X-Auth-Email/X-Auth-Key headers. OAuth clients (authorization_code) can be created self-serve in the dashboard, but the OAuth docs show limited scopes (e.g. workers-platform), and the evidence does not show it covering the whole API. API token is therefore primary. The OTHER entry is a weak placeholder for the legacy email+key header scheme.
access_notes: Any Cloudflare account can create API tokens from the dashboard. Free-plan zones are supported. Some features (API Shield, Tenant/partner API) need Enterprise or a partner agreement, but the core API does not.
blocker_notes: No blocker for the core API. Tenant/partner and API Shield features are gated, but they are not needed for a toolkit.

evidence.quote: Cloudflare uses the RFC standardAuthorization: Bearer <Token> interface.
From the [Cloudflare dashboard ↗︎](https://dash.cloudflare.com/profile/api-tokens/), go to **My Profile** > **API Tokens** for user tokens.
To create an OAuth client, you must have one of these roles for the associated account: Super Administrator, Administrator, or OAuth Client Write.
A token-efficient MCP server for the entire Cloudflare API. 2500 endpoints in 1k tokens
